{{Short description|French physicist (born 1952)}}
'''Serge Galam''' (born 1952) is a French [[physicist]] and Scientist Emeritus at [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chercheurs émérites|url=http://www.sciencespo.fr/cevipof/fr/equipe/academic-staff/Chercheurs%20%C3%A9m%C3%A9rites|date=2020-06-01|publisher=SciencesPO|access-date=2020-06-01}}</ref>

== Biography ==
In 1975, Serge Galam obtained a PhD in physics at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in Paris. In 1981, he received a [[Ph.D.]] in physics at [[Tel Aviv University]]. From 1981 to 1983, he taught at [[City University of New York]] and from 1983 to 1985 at [[New York University]].

From 1984 to 2004, he worked in several physics laboratories of the Pierre and Marie Curie University.

In 1999, he was appointed director of research at the [[CNRS|Centre national de la recherche scientifique]].

In 2004 he joined the [[Centre de Recherche en Epistémologie Appliquée|Center for Research in Applied Epistemology]] of the [[École Polytechnique]] (CREA). In 2013, he joined the faculty of [[Sciences Po]].

Serge Galam is one of the pioneers of the modern field of [[Social physics|sociophysics]].<ref name="Galam2012">{{harv| Galam |2012 | id=Galam2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Review|url=http://jasss.soc.surrey.ac.uk/16/2/reviews/2.html|author=Cesar Garcia-Diaz|agency=JASSS|language=en|year=2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sociophysique, ultra-brève introduction|url=https://rhubarbe.net/2009/08/03/sociophysique-ultra-breve-introduction/|author=Vincent Verschoore|access-date=22 January 2017|date=2009-08-03}}</ref> His work focuses on the dynamics of group decision making and how minority opinions can sway public opinion. In the fall of 2016, using the principles of sociophysics, Galam predicted the election of [[Donald Trump]],<ref>{{cite journal |last=Galam |first=Serge |arxiv=1609.03933|title=The Trump phenomenon, an explanation from sociophysics |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics B |volume=31 |issue=10 |page=1742015 |date=13 Sep 2016 |doi=10.1142/S0217979217420152 |s2cid=118507351 }}</ref> although he would incorrectly predict Trump's reelection in the fall of 2020.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Galam |first=Serge |arxiv=2010.10602|title=Will Trump win again in the 2020 election? An answer from a sociophysics model |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |volume=570 |article-number=125835 |date=May 2021 |doi=10.1016/j.physa.2021.125835 |bibcode=2021PhyA..57025835G |s2cid=224814211 }}</ref>
